Aa

Macrons

Consonantal i

Consonantal u

Theme

Civic life: news, government & the law

assault noun

also assault and battery, battery, attack (on a person), commit assault, accuse of assault, violence

classical

Cic. Phil. 2.4: dē vī condemnātī sunt (Lewis & Short s.v. vīs)
Traupman 193

vīs, vim, vī f.

violence, assault

Only the accusative vim and the ablative vī are common in the singular; the charge of assault is dē vī.

Examples

  • vim facere in aliquem

    to commit assault against someoneTraupman 193; cf. Cic. Caecin. 63: inermibus vim facere (Lewis & Short s.v. inermis)

  • alicui vim afferre

    to assault someoneTraupman 191

  • aliquem dē vī (et manū) accūsāre

    to accuse someone of assault (and battery)Traupman 193; cf. Cic. Sest. 75: dē vī reus (Lewis & Short s.v. reus)

See also attack, beat up, charge.

SourcesLewis & Short: vis

John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 191, 193.
